questions.q: According to the New Automation screen's own descriptions, which of these flow types does NOT describe itself as running as an autolaunched flow in the background?
options: Screen Flow
Record-Triggered Flow
Schedule-Triggered Flow
Autolaunched Flow (No Trigger)
questions.explain: Screen Flow is the one flow type in this chapter built around a user watching a screen — the others all describe themselves as running in the background.

questions.q: In Setup's Flows list filtered to Autolaunched Flows, what does a row with a blank Trigger column indicate?
options: The flow is broken and cannot be activated
The flow is an Autolaunched Flow (No Trigger) — nothing built-in starts it automatically
The flow is a Screen Flow mistakenly filtered into the list
The flow runs only in a sandbox
questions.explain: A blank Trigger means there's no schedule, record save, or platform event wired to the Start element — it's a true Autolaunched Flow (No Trigger).

questions.q: Per its own description on the New Flow screen, what launches an Autolaunched Flow (No Trigger)?
options: A platform event message only
A record being created, updated, or deleted
A specified date and time
Invocation by Apex, processes, REST API, and more
questions.explain: Its description reads: "Launches when invoked by Apex, processes, REST API, and more. This autolaunched flow runs in the background."

questions.q: What does a custom button's Content Source set to URL accomplish, as shown in this lesson?
options: It deletes the flow after one run
It converts the flow into a screen flow
It points the button at the flow's URL, passing values in as parameters — a user-driven way to invoke it
It schedules the flow to run nightly
questions.explain: A classic custom button with Content Source: URL can point at an autolaunched flow's URL and pass input values as query parameters when clicked.

questions.q: True or false: an Autolaunched Flow (No Trigger) can skip activation if it's only ever called by Apex.
options: False — every flow, including this type, must be activated before anything can run it
True — Apex-invoked flows bypass activation
True, but only in a sandbox org
False, but only because Apex requires a screen element
questions.explain: Activation is required regardless of how a flow gets invoked; an inactive flow can't be run by Apex, a button, or anything else.
